title: Proactive Synthetic Probing and Cost‑Aware Ejection Policy for Canary Failures
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a proactive ejection policy driven by synthetic probing that combines latency, error rate, throughput and token cost into a single weighted signal. The policy should detect regressions before user traffic is widely affected, avoid flapping via hysteresis counters, and prioritize cost-sensitive workloads. This ticket covers the algorithm, probe harness, dashboard surfaces, and staged rollout plan for canaries and A/B experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic probe harness can run against canary variants with configurable traffic mix and prompt templates
Weighted signal composed from p95 latency, error rate, and per-request token cost is computed every minute and stored in metrics lake
Ejection decision triggers when weighted signal exceeds adaptive threshold for 3 consecutive windows (configurable) and automatically shifts traffic to fallback model
Hysteresis prevents immediate re-admit for at least 10 minutes, configurable per-project
Dashboards show probe results, contributing metric breakdown, and decision rationale; alerts fire with links to change and probe traces
Offline replay on historical production traces demonstrates >90% detection rate for injected regressions with <2% false positive rate across three workload archetypes
technical_design: We will implement a small fleet of synthetic probe workers that issue short representative prompts sampled from per-customer workload classes. Each probe run produces metrics: latency (ms), success boolean (error types), tokens_out, tokens_in, and throughput. For each canary cohort we compute a per-minute composite score: score = w_latency * norm(p95_latency) + w_error * norm(error_rate) + w_cost * norm(avg_tokens_per_req) + w_throughput * norm(throughput_penalty). Norm() maps to a robust z-like score using a rolling median and MAD to reduce sensitivity to outliers. We use quantile baselining: expected distribution computed from control (current prod) and stored as baseline. The adaptive threshold is baseline + k * MAD. We allow per-customer or per-project weight overrides. The ejection controller maintains a small state machine per-canary: observe -> warn -> eject -> cooldown -> allow-retry. Ejection occurs only if score>threshold for N consecutive windows and at least one of the following holds: rapid token-cost delta (>10%), p95 latency regression above relative threshold, or error-rate absolute threshold exceeded. Ejections are soft by default (shift 80% traffic away) and can be configured to immediate full rollback for P0 incidents. To avoid flapping we implement a cooldown timer and escalate to manual revoke if repeated ejections occur within 1 hour. All decisions are logged with contributing metric weights and recent probe traces for auditability.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Offline simulation — run probe harness on replay of 30 days of production traffic and inject synthetic regressions to estimate detection/false positive trade-offs
Phase 1: Canary-only probes — enable probes for internal canaries (green-team) with alerting to oncall; use soft ejects (step-down) only
Phase 2: Expanded canaries — enable for customer canaries with opt-in, exercise cohort-specific weighting, collect metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 3: Auto-eject enabled — enable auto-eject with conservative thresholds; monitor for false positives and adjust weights
Phase 4: Default rollout — flip to enabled for all new canaries with ability to opt-out per release
tasks: Build probe worker service (k8s job) and template prompt sets per workload archetype
Add composite signal computation in metrics pipeline (Prometheus + materialized view)
Implement ejection controller with state machine and audit logging
Add dashboard tiles for probe health, signal breakdown, and recent ejection events
Integrate alert rules and runbook entry; update oncall rotation docs
Run offline replay tests and create evaluation report
comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Patel: Initial draft of design. Focused on combining cost into the decision to help Dedicated customers avoid silent cost regressions.
2025-02-18 Liam O'Connor: Added hysteresis counters and soft-eject option after discussing concern about flapping in low-traffic canaries.
2025-02-25 Data Team (review): Suggested using MAD-based normalization vs mean/std to be robust to spikes; updated technical design accordingly.
2025-03-03 Security (review): No sensitive data in probe payloads; recommend scrubbing or using hashed prompt ids in logs. Marked security_review_required=false.
2025-03-05 Maya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria with offline replay thresholds and added cooldown policy per PM feedback.
notes: Measurement windows are intentionally short (1 minute) for early detection; balance with sample noise via consecutive-window requirement
Cost weighting is critical for Dedicated customers on fixed budgets — ops should be able to lower w_cost for latency-critical tiers
We should expose a sandbox UI for SREs to run ad-hoc probe runs against arbitrary model versions
Future: explore Bayesian change-point detection to replace simple consecutive-window logic if we see high variance workloads
